title: Forward (Filmmakers in Attendance for Q&A)

title: FIGHT! FIGHT! FIGHT!

title: Paper Flowers – Special Presentation

title: Let It Be Done: The Fiat Echoes Still
description: An original musical feature produced by St. Mary's Parish that weaves Mary's biblical journey with modern generational struggles of identity, doubt, and purpose. Through drama and original music, the production explores timeless themes of courage, faith, and saying yes.

title: Travis Holp: Life After Life Live
description: Join internationally known medium and author Travis Holp as he delivers messages from loved ones in spirit to audience members. Blending heart, insight, and evidential messages, this live evening offers comfort, healing, and connection.

title: Susan Rice

title: John Muirhead
description: MRG LIVE presents Toronto-based singer-songwriter John Muirhead crafting big-hearted indie-folk songs alongside Sarah Vanderzon. Touring in support of his music and upcoming album, John brings his storytelling and heartfelt melodies to the Fox Cabaret.

title: 90s vs 00s Night
description: The Fox Cabaret presents a throwback dance battle of the decades featuring Common People DJs playing hits from the 90s and 00s. Attendees can dance the night away to decide whether the 1990s or 2000s reigns supreme.

title: Centre Stage
description: Stanley Kwan's 1991 biographical masterpiece chronicles the tragic final years of Chinese silent film icon Ruan Lingyu, played by Maggie Cheung. This 35th anniversary engagement presents a stunning 4K restoration exploring fame, artistic identity, and historical melodrama.

title: Royal Space Force: The Wings of Honnêamise
description: Studio Gainax's ambitious 1987 debut feature follows an alternate-future military space branch volunteer pilot through an anti-drama space-race odyssey. Screened in a new restoration featuring a masterwork score by Sakamoto Ryuichi.

title: Tokyo Melody: A Film About Ryuichi Sakamoto
description: A restored 1985 documentary by Elizabeth Lennard capturing electronic-music pioneer Ryuichi Sakamoto during the recording of Ongaku Zukan amid the bustling streets of Bubble-era Tokyo. Screened at The Cinematheque in Japanese with English subtitles.

title: When I Walk
description: Winner of an Emmy for Outstanding Informational Programming, When I Walk is an intimate autobiographical documentary following filmmaker Jason DaSilva as he navigates life after being diagnosed with multiple sclerosis. Hosted by Harry Killas in support of ECU 100, the screening will be followed by a reflection and Q&A with DaSilva.

title: Can you make us a music video? Owen Ellis ft. YEP
description: A celebration of Vancouver's DIY music scene showcasing music videos by local filmmaker Owen Ellis. Features a post-screening Q&A moderated by Casey Wei followed by a live musical performance by YEP.

title: Macunaíma
description: Joaquim Pedro de Andrade’s absurdist Cinema Novo classic follows the satirical adventures of Macunaíma across Brazil. Presented as part of UBC's 'Cinema Thinks the World' series, this free screening is followed by a reception and panel discussion.

title: Honouring Our Warriors: Forgotten Warriors & Cree Code Talker
description: This program honours First Nations, Métis, and Inuit veterans with screenings of Alexandra Lazarowich's Cree Code Talker and Loretta Todd's Forgotten Warriors. The evening features an in-person post-screening Q&A with director Loretta Todd.

title: Blue Road: The Edna O’Brien Story
description: Sinéad O’Shea's empathetic documentary offers a candid reflection on the extraordinary life and literary legacy of Irish author Edna O’Brien. Drawing from personal journals narrated by Jessie Buckley alongside testimonials from fellow artists, the film celebrates O'Brien's fearless creative spirit.

title: Julie Keeps Quiet
description: As the star player at an elite tennis academy, Julie's life revolves around the game she loves until her coach falls under investigation following a teammate's suicide. Faced with a culture of silence, Julie must decide whether speaking out will jeopardize her promising tennis career.

title: European Union Film Festival 2026: Our Girls
description: Oscar winner Mike van Diem delivers a tense, character-driven drama about trust, parenthood, and long-standing friendship unraveling after an Alpine accident involving teenage daughters. Screening as part of the European Union Film Festival 2026 at The Cinematheque with online streaming options.

title: The Dance Club
description: Screening as part of the European Union Film Festival 2026, Lisa Langseth's social-critique comedy follows a psych student who launches a dance program to restore embodied self-connection for his clients. The Swedish feature stars Nils Wetterholm alongside standout actor Alva Bratt.

title: Receptions
description: Filippos Tsitos's delectably dark tragicomedy follows an unemployed Athens journalist who begins sneaking into high-society parties to survive hunger and homelessness. Screening as part of the European Union Film Festival 2026 at The Cinematheque.

title: Popeye Meets Sindbad the Sailor and More Fleischer Cartoons
description: A Film Club presentation marking 90 years since Popeye Meets Sindbad the Sailor, featuring a 71-minute selection of restored, inventive Fleischer studio animation shorts. Screened at The Cinematheque in downtown Vancouver.

title: Spiked
description: Holly, a spirited young hedgehog sheltered by her father, teams up with an exhausted rabbit who believes he is a legendary warrior hero after a collision. Caroline Origer's charming animated adventure pairs lively visual slapstick with a tender story about stepping outside your comfort zone.

title: Chopin, a Sonata in Paris
description: Director Michał Kwieciński presents a kinetic biographical drama uncovering the fragile, tempestuous genius of Fryderyk Chopin in 1830s Paris. Anchored by Eryk Kulm's magnetic lead performance, the film explores the young virtuoso's meteoric rise amidst chronic illness and artistic pressure.

title: European Union Film Festival 2026: My Family and Other Clowns
description: A documentary portrait exploring the delicate balance between performance and parenting for two world-renowned Estonian clowns. Directed by Heilika Pikkov and Liina Särkinen as part of the European Union Film Festival.

title: Sleeping with a Tiger
description: Sleeping with a Tiger blends documentary and stylish fiction to explore the life and career of celebrated Austrian painter Maria Lassnig. Directed by Anja Salomonowitz and starring Birgit Minichmayr, the film portrays Lassnig's radical artistic vision and determination in a male-dominated art world.

title: Borderline
description: Acclaimed director Ignas Jonynas presents a razor-sharp psychological thriller following a solitary ornithologist entangled in a dangerous border-smuggling syndicate while raising his neurodivergent daughter. Screening as part of the European Union Film Festival 2026 at The Cinematheque.

title: Romzsa Tódor
description: Set against the turbulent backdrop of World War II and its aftermath, this powerful biographical drama chronicles the life and martyrdom of Transcarpathian Greek Catholic bishop Romzsa Tódor. Directed by Attila Bokor, the film screens as part of the European Union Film Festival.

title: Castillo
description: In this rich adaptation of Clare Azzopardi’s novel directed by Abigail Mallia, a complex mystery grounded in Malta’s turbulent political past unfolds as Amanda investigates her family secrets. Real-world trauma and the fictional universe of Inspector Castillo collide to reveal buried truths.

title: Green Light
description: Director Pavel Cuzuioc follows Dr. Johann Spittler, a German neuropsychiatrist evaluating patients seeking assisted dying, while facing his own manslaughter trial. The Canadian Premiere screening is followed by a discussion with MAID assessor and provider Elizabeth Leonardis.

title: Still Afloat
description: Part of the European Union Film Festival 2026, Gonzaga Manso's debut feature Still Afloat is an affectionate, patient tribute to his grandfather and Spanish cinema icon Saturnino García. The film explores aging, autonomy, and memory as an elderly fisherman navigates his final summer routines.

title: Life Is Life
description: Set on the eve of the millennium, Life Is Life follows a Milanese businessman attempting to build a luxury resort on Sardinia and an elderly shepherd refusing to sell his ancestral land. Directed by Riccardo Milani, this warm David and Goliath comedy screens as part of the European Union Film Festival.

title: Stereo Girls
description: In 1992 South of France, inseparable high school friends Charlotte and Liza dream of conquering Paris with their synth-pop songs. When tragedy strikes, Charlotte must navigate grief and dreams in this moving drama about friendship, love, and loss.

title: Rose
description: Part of the European Union Film Festival 2026, this Danish family drama directed by Niels Arden Oplev follows sisters Inger and Ellen on a life-changing bus journey to Paris. Sofie Gråbøl delivers a powerful performance as Inger in an exploration of identity and mental illness.

title: Hold Onto Me
description: Eleven-year-old Iris reconnects with her estranged scam-artist father Aris after getting into trouble, forming an unlikely team until his past catches up with them. Screened as part of the European Union Film Festival 2026 at The Cinematheque.

title: Family Time
description: In Tia Kouvo's sparkling, bittersweet debut dramedy, an ordinary Finnish family reunites over the Christmas holidays with humor, friction, and poignant observation. Screening in-person as part of the European Union Film Festival 2026 at The Cinematheque, accompanied by an online streaming window.

title: 3.0 Kilograms of Happiness
description: Screening as part of the European Union Film Festival 2026, this comedy-family drama from director Zornitsa Sophia follows a 55-year-old mother who decides to carry an embryo for her struggling daughter. Based on a true Bulgarian story, the film navigates a chaotic clash of family dynamics, ethics, and love.

title: Escape Net
description: Set in Soviet-era Riga, Dzintars Dreibergs directs a sports drama following a spirited teenager whose passion for basketball fuels the birth of TTT Riga. The film captures the quiet resilience of a team and nation navigating KGB surveillance during the Soviet era.

title: The Secret of Pin-Up Island
description: An all-woman cast fronts this whimsical, honey-coloured sci-fi fantasy set at the intersection of therapy and AI-frontier technology. Rina Gri stars as a patient undergoing an immersive virtual reality treatment for depression powered by a personalized AI engine.

title: The Portuguese
description: In the prelude to the Carnation Revolution, two men fleeing their homeland share their struggles in this musical portrait of Portugal directed by Vicente Alves do Ó. Across thirteen song-anchored stories, the film presents an ambitious and prismatic chronicle of Portuguese history and identity.

title: Dražen
description: Dražen is a compelling biographical drama following Croatian basketball icon Dražen Petrović, chronicling his rise from Yugoslavia to the NBA and the 1992 Olympic final against the US Dream Team. Directed by Danilo Šerbedžija, the film delves into his complex personal life, passion for the sport, and rebellious spirit.

title: Invincibles
description: Screening as part of the European Union Film Festival 2026, Invincibles is a moving sports drama inspired by true stories from the 2019 World Para Ice Hockey Championships in Ostrava. Director Dan Pánek combines heartfelt emotion and humour to tell an uplifting tale of determination and second chances.

title: Impatience of the Heart
description: Writer-director Lauro Cress transposes Stefan Zweig's novel into an intense psychological drama about empathy, guilt, and human connection. Screening as part of the European Union Film Festival 2026 at The Cinematheque.

title: The Dormant Account
description: Veteran Slovak filmmaker Miloslav Luther directs this gripping historical drama following a couple who uncover a dark wartime family secret after attempting to sell an inherited painting. Screening as part of the European Union Film Festival 2026 at The Cinematheque.

title: Hidden People
description: Guti and Sig wake up hung over and handcuffed together in this heartwarmingly absurd buddy comedy exploring loneliness and belonging. Directed by Miha Hočevar, the pair start planning to build a river raft and float downstream on society's outskirts.

title: Traces
description: Part of the European Union Film Festival, Traces documents the courage and resilience of Ukrainian women surviving conflict-related violence as they transform collective trauma into mutual support. Proceeds from this special screening benefit the Canada–Ukraine Foundation.

title: Cairo Station
description: The culmination of Youssef Chahine’s first decade of filmmaking, Cairo Station is a rush of sweat, tears, and encroaching shadow set around the bustling Cairo central rail hub. Presented as part of the 'Endless Desire: Youssef Chahine at 100' retrospective in a new restoration, preceded by the short Cairo as Seen by Chahine.

title: Moving Histories: DAVRA
description: “Moving Histories” brings together cinematic works by five women artists exploring family narratives, displacement, and regional filmmaking in Central Asia. The screening includes an in-person conversation with filmmaker Zumrad Mirzalieva moderated by Althea Thauberger.

title: The Host
description: Bong Joon Ho's critically acclaimed creature feature follows a dysfunctional family attempting to rescue their daughter from a giant mutant monster terrorizing the Han River. Screened in a stunning new restoration at The Cinematheque.

title: Program One: Figure and Ground
description: Four standout works by pioneering avant-garde filmmaker Gunvor Nelson screening on 16mm prints and digital formats as part of her Personal Films retrospective. Highlights include Take Off, Light Years Expanding, Moons Pool, and My Name Is Oona.

title: Dawn of a New Day
description: Youssef Chahine's second colour feature blends Sirkian melodrama with post-revolution Cairo social realism as a fortysomething socialite enters an unexpected May–December romance. Screened as part of The Cinematheque's centenary retrospective 'Endless Desire: Youssef Chahine at 100'.

title: The Double Life of Véronique
description: Krzysztof Kieślowski's haunting and luminous metaphysical fable follows two physically identical women living parallel lives in Poland and France. Irène Jacob won Best Actress at Cannes for her captivating dual performance exploring fate, music, and mysterious connection.

title: The Land (الأرض)
description: Youssef Chahine's masterpiece portrays a collective group of 1930s Egyptian villagers fighting against oppressive authorities who threaten to cut off their water supply. Presented as part of the Endless Desire: Youssef Chahine at 100 series at The Cinematheque in Arabic with English subtitles.

title: The Calm
description: Part of the series Wheel of Fortune: The Films of Krzysztof Kieślowski, The Calm follows ex-con Antek as his modest aspirations clash with workplace solidarity during an illegal strike. Screened on DCP with English subtitles at The Cinematheque.

title: The Scar
description: Krzysztof Kieślowski's debut theatrical feature follows a project manager overseeing a controversial chemical factory construction in his hometown. Screened as part of the Wheel of Fortune retrospective in Polish with English subtitles.

title: Gangsterism
description: Filmmaker Isiah Medina returns to DIM Cinema for the Vancouver premiere of his sartorial cinéma à clef and avant-garde gangster feature Gangsterism. The screening is followed by an in-person Q&A with director Isiah Medina moderated by programmer Steff Huì Cí Ling.

title: Another Round
description: In Thomas Vinterberg's existential dramedy Another Round, four teachers test the theory that maintaining a slight blood-alcohol level enhances creativity and daily life. Presented as part of the 'Cinema Thinks the World' series, this free screening is followed by a reception and a one-hour panel discussion.

title: Christmas at Moose Factory / Remaining Native
description: Part of the Our Stories to Tell series, this double bill pairs Alanis Obomsawin's iconic Christmas at Moose Factory with Paige Bethmann's SXSW award-winning documentary Remaining Native. Both films connect stories across Turtle Island through an enduring love for land, family, and Indigenous culture.

title: Put Your Soul on Your Hand and Walk
description: Put Your Soul on Your Hand and Walk offers an intimate portrait of daily life in Gaza through video calls between exiled Iranian filmmaker Sepideh Farsi and young Palestinian photojournalist Fatma Hassona. The screening will be followed by a post-screening audience discussion moderated by Pelan.

title: Adieu Bonaparte
description: Set during Napoleon’s late-18th-century occupation of Egypt, Youssef Chahine’s Adieu Bonaparte explores the complex, coercive relationship between a French military officer and two Egyptian brothers. Presented as part of the 'Endless Desire: Youssef Chahine at 100' retrospective at The Cinematheque.

title: Cameron Winter at Carnegie Hall
description: Directed and shot on 35mm and 16mm by Paul Thomas Anderson, this concert documentary captures Geese frontman Cameron Winter's landmark solo performance at Carnegie Hall. The 72-minute film memorializes an electrifying and historic evening celebrating his acclaimed solo work.

title: Kieślowski Documentaries × 6
description: A curated program of six rarely screened short documentaries by Polish director Krzysztof Kieślowski screening as part of the Wheel of Fortune retrospective. Spanning from 1966 to 1990, these works examine everyday bureaucracy and social groupings across Poland.

title: Camera Buff
description: A wry satirical comedy about artistic expression and political oppression, Camera Buff marked Krzysztof Kieślowski’s international breakthrough. The film follows a factory clerk who becomes obsessed with his new 8mm camera, making industrial documentaries that clash with officialdom and censorship.

title: Program Two: Mother and Daughter
description: Gunvor Nelson’s interest in the varieties of experience for women across generations and social roles is highlighted in these two 16mm works, featuring Kirsa Nicholina and Red Shift. Together, they explore domestic space, personal memory, and the nuanced relationships between mothers and daughters.

title: I Swear
description: Set in mid-’80s Scotland, I Swear dramatizes the adolescence and early adulthood of Tourette’s Syndrome advocate John Davidson with empathy and humor. The screening is followed by an insightful discussion with Dr. Anton Scamvougeras.

title: That Day on the Beach
description: Edward Yang’s auspicious 1983 theatrical debut stands as a milestone in Taiwanese cinema, exploring modernity, tradition, and the position of women through layered storytelling. Starring Sylvia Chang and featuring early cinematography by Christopher Doyle, this new restoration screens as part of The Cinematheque's Essential Big Screen series.

title: The Misfits
description: John Huston directs Marilyn Monroe, Clark Gable, and Montgomery Clift in Arthur Miller's poignant 1961 Nevada desert drama about drifting souls seeking reinvention. Presented in a new digital restoration as part of The Cinematheque's Essential Big Screen series.

title: Blind Chance
description: In Krzysztof Kieślowski’s innovative narrative, a young medical student rushes to catch a train and faces three divergent destinies illustrating chance, fate, and political reality in Poland. Screening as part of the Wheel of Fortune: The Films of Krzysztof Kieślowski series at The Cinematheque.

title: Three Colours: Blue
description: Krzysztof Kieślowski's masterwork stars Juliette Binoche as a woman rebuilding her life following a tragic family loss. The metaphysical drama explores grief and emotional liberation through stunning cinematography and evocative music.

title: The Tales of Hoffmann
description: Michael Powell and Emeric Pressburger's sumptuous 1951 film adaptation blends opera, ballet, and expressionistic cinema based on Jacques Offenbach's fantastical work. Presented as part of the Essential Big Screen series in a full-length restoration featuring performances by Moira Shearer and Léonide Massine.

title: Rex: A Dinosaur’s Story
description: Japanese blockbuster Rex: A Dinosaur’s Story tells the charming tale of a lonely girl who forms a bond with a newly hatched dinosaur in rural Tokachi. Directed by Kadokawa Haruki with animatronics by Carlo Rambaldi, this restored classic is presented as part of The Cinematheque's Film Club.

title: No End
description: Krzysztof Kieślowski’s poignant political ghost story follows a deceased lawyer observing his grieving widow and former client amidst martial-law Poland. Screening as part of the Wheel of Fortune retrospective at The Cinematheque in Polish with English subtitles.

title: Three Colours: White
description: The second installment in Krzysztof Kieślowski’s Three Colours trilogy, White is a dryly comic tale of heartbreak, pride, and bittersweet revenge set between Paris and Poland. Screened at The Cinematheque as part of the Wheel of Fortune retrospective series.

title: The Piano
description: Jane Campion's Palme d'Or-winning masterpiece follows mute Scottish woman Ada and her daughter Flora after they arrive in 19th-century New Zealand. A sensual, Brontëan tale of passion and fury presented in a new restoration.

title: A Short Film About Love
description: A 19-year-old postal worker in Warsaw becomes obsessed with his older neighbour, spying on her before initiating contact in Krzysztof Kieślowski's taut masterpiece. The darkly ironic yet deeply romantic study of intimacy and voyeurism expands upon an episode from the director's Dekalog series.

title: A Short Film About Killing
description: Krzysztof Kieślowski's Cannes Jury Prize–winning masterpiece expands on his Dekalog series to examine crime and capital punishment in 1980s Warsaw. Presented in Polish with English subtitles as part of the retrospective series Wheel of Fortune: The Films of Krzysztof Kieślowski.

title: Three Colours: Red
description: The concluding chapter of Krzysztof Kieślowski’s Three Colours trilogy explores fraternity, chance, and destiny when a young Swiss model crosses paths with a retired judge. Presented in French with English subtitles at The Cinematheque in downtown Vancouver.

title: Marketa Lazarová
description: František Vláčil’s monumental Czech medieval epic Marketa Lazarová screens in a new restoration at The Cinematheque. Set in 13th-century Europe at the clash of paganism and Christianity, the film follows the kidnapped daughter of clan Lazar in a visually dazzling, feral cinematic masterpiece.

title: Morvern Callar
description: Lynne Ramsay directs Samantha Morton in this sensory adaptation of Alan Warner's novel about a young woman navigating grief, liberation, and deception after a sudden tragedy. Screened in a new digital restoration as part of The Cinematheque's Essential Big Screen series.

title: Dekalog
description: Krzysztof Kieślowski's monumental ten-part cinematic masterpiece Dekalog explores complex moral dilemmas inspired by the Ten Commandments through Warsaw housing project residents. Screened in paired parts as part of The Cinematheque's retrospective Wheel of Fortune: The Films of Krzysztof Kieślowski.

title: Free First Friday Nights
description: Experience the Vancouver Art Gallery during Free First Friday Nights presented by BMO with complimentary admission from 4 to 8 PM. Visitors can explore current exhibitions and gallery collections with advance reserved tickets.

title: Member Tour and Book Signing: Richard Hill on That Green Ideal
description: Join Richard Hill, Senior Curator of Canadian Art, for an exclusive Members-only tour of the exhibition That Green Ideal: Emily Carr and the Idea of Nature. Following the gallery tour, a book signing will be hosted in front of the Gallery Store.

title: Artist Talk: Jean Shin
description: Artist Jean Shin explores the intersection of technology, material consumption, and environmental change in conjunction with the exhibition Future Geographies. The talk is followed by a conversation with UBC professors Dr. Sara Ghebremusse and Dr. Milind Kandlikar.

title: The Making Place | Collage and Sound Sculptures
description: Drop in to Room 4East at the Vancouver Art Gallery for hands-on, educator-led artmaking inspired by exhibitions That Green Ideal: Emily Carr and the Idea of Nature and Emily Hermant's wire compositions. The program is included with standard gallery admission, featuring a special guided Family Tour at 2 PM for visitors aged 5 to 12 and their families.

title: The Making Place | Yarn Compositions and Paper Animal Sculptures
description: Drop into Room 4East at the Vancouver Art Gallery for hands-on art-making featuring yarn compositions and paper animal sculptures inspired by collection artists. Activities and guided 2:00 PM family tours are included with standard gallery admission, with free entry for youth 18 and under.

title: The Making Place | Wire Compositions and Collage
description: Drop in every Sunday to explore hands-on art-making activities led by Gallery Art Educators in Room 4East, with wire compositions and collage inspired by current exhibitions. Participation is included with general gallery admission and features a guided family tour at 2 PM.

title: The Making Place | Stapler Scenes and Hard-Edge Painting
description: Drop in to Room 4East at the Vancouver Art Gallery for hands-on art-making activities inspired by current exhibitions, including stapler scenes and hard-edge painting. Included with general gallery admission, the family-friendly event also features an optional guided family tour at 2 PM.

title: Social Series
venue: Arts Club Theatre Company (Granville Island Stage)
description: Arts Club Theatre Company's Social Series brings community gathering spaces for local creatives and members back to life. The ongoing series features Broadway Open Mics, Scratch Nights for playwrights, and cabaret evenings.

title: Young Creators Company
venue: Arts Club Theatre Company (Granville Island Stage)
description: The Young Creators Company invites youth in grades 7–12 to collaboratively create and perform an original theatrical showcase over a 12-week program. Guided by professional teaching artists at Arts Club rehearsal studios, participants explore acting, comedy, scriptwriting, directing, and stagecraft.

title: Directing 101
venue: Arts Club Theatre Company (Granville Island Stage)
description: Directing 101 is an adult education course presented by Arts Club Theatre Company. The session is scheduled for March 22, 2027 with registration available online.

title: Summer, 1976
venue: Arts Club Theatre Company (Granville Island Stage)
description: During one extraordinary summer, free-spirited housewife Alice and serious single mother Diana forge an unlikely bond while their young daughters play. Written by David Auburn, this moving memory play explores the profound and lasting impact of female friendship.

title: Louisa May Alcott's Little Women
venue: Arts Club Theatre Company (Granville Island Stage)
description: Arts Club Theatre Company presents an on-tour theatrical adaptation of Louisa May Alcott's classic novel Little Women. The production follows the lives and ambitions of the March sisters across multiple upcoming February performances.

title: Winter Trout Fest & Pancake Lunch
description: Celebrate winter at Trout Lake Community Centre with free skating, children's activities, crafts, and a bouncy castle play gym. Guests can also enjoy an optional $5 pancake lunch with sausages and fruit across two reserved seatings.

title: Pottery, Bake, Quilt, Knit Sale
description: The semi-annual pottery, bake, quilt, and knit sale features one-of-a-kind handmade creations and delicious homemade treats. Admission is free with no registration required in the Trout Lake Community Centre lobby.

title: Comic Maker Meet-Up
description: A weekly community meet-up presented in partnership with Cloudscape Comics connecting Vancouver cartoonists of all skill levels. Attendees participate in short introductions followed by open discussion, sharing, and drawing sessions.

title: 2026 BC Achievement FNA + AAD Combined Exhibition
description: A combined exhibition showcasing artworks by the 2026 recipients of the Sam Carter Award in Applied Art + Design and the Polygon Award in First Nations Art. Held at The Roundhouse Exhibition Hall, this free event shares knowledge, dialogue, and community connection through local art and innovation.

title: Songbird North
description: Hosted and produced by Shari Ulrich, Songbird North is a bi-monthly showcase featuring four singer-songwriters playing songs and sharing stories together on stage. This edition features performances by Dante Hadden, Chris Ronald, and Brandon Wolfe Scott alongside Ulrich at the Roundhouse.

title: Portobello West Holiday Market
description: Portobello West Holiday Market returns to the Roundhouse Community Arts & Recreation Centre in Vancouver for a two-day festive artisan shopping experience. Browse curated local creators, designers, and handcrafted goods.

title: Concord Christmas
description: Celebrate the holiday season at the Roundhouse with photos with Santa, live entertainment, cookie decorating, holiday crafts, face painting, and festive lights. Bring the entire family to enjoy hot chocolate and community festivities, with entry offered by donation.

title: Gingerbread House Decorating
description: Build an extra festive gingerbread house with all supplies, kits, hot chocolate, and marshmallows provided. Families and groups can bring as many people as they like per registered kit in the Exhibition Hall.

title: Breakfast or Brunch with Santa
description: Join Santa and his helpers at the Roundhouse for pancake brunch, cookie decorating, arts & crafts, and live music. Parent participation is required for this family holiday gathering.

title: Merry, Gay, & Bright
description: Explore a curated queer market featuring handcrafted artisanal goods, innovative art, and design from the local 2SLGBTQIA+ community. Guests can also enjoy high-energy performances from a sensational lineup of drag artists celebrating self-expression.

title: 33rd Annual Winter Solstice Festival
description: Presented in partnership with the Secret Lantern Society, the 33rd Annual Winter Solstice Festival honors the longest night of the year with community lanterns, the Labyrinth of Light, and an 8:00 PM family walk. Attendees can join lantern-making workshops leading up to the evening celebration at the Roundhouse Performance Centre and Exhibition Hall.

title: Vancouver Canadians vs. Tri-City Dust Devils
venue: Scotiabank Field at Nat Bailey Stadium
description: Minor League Baseball action featuring the Vancouver Canadians hosting Northwest League opponents at Rogers Field at Nat Bailey Stadium. Fans can enjoy outdoor professional baseball games with afternoon and evening matchups throughout the homestand.

title: Saturday Night Stand Up Comedy
description: Saturday Night Stand Up Comedy features live stand-up performances at Comedy After Dark in Gastown. Seating is first-come, first-served general admission with full bar and kitchen service available.

title: Ballet Jörgen’s Swan Lake
description: Celebrate Ballet Jörgen's 25th anniversary with a breathtaking new interpretation of Swan Lake, reimagined along the rugged shores of the Fortress of Louisbourg in Nova Scotia. Artistic Director Bengt Jörgen blends the timeless beauty of the beloved ballet with Canadian heritage, creating a fresh take on the classic story. Featuring stunning sets by Camellia Koo, authentic 17th-century-inspired costumes, and world-class choreography, this captivating production offers a uniquely Canadian perspective on one of ballet's most cherished masterpieces.

title: RuPaul's Drag Race Werq The World News
description: To celebrate its 10-year anniversary, RuPaul's Drag Race Werq The World Tour returns with WTWN 10: Werq The World News, a high-camp global broadcast hosted by Asia O’Hara. The live production features reports and performances from drag favorites including Vanessa Vanjie, Jorgeous, Latrice Royale, Daya Betty, and Shannel.

title: International Guitar Night
description: The world's premier touring acoustic guitar festival brings four celebrated guitarists spanning classical, flamenco, jazz, and world music to the Massey Theatre. This year's lineup features Itamar Erez, Victoria Ruiz de la Rubia, Cenk Erdoğan, and Remi Harris.

title: Silent Movie Mondays: 2026
description: Escape to the 1920s silent movie era at the historic Orpheum with classic films accompanied by live music on the original Wurlitzer organ. The evening features a pre-show performance by the Gatsby Strutters Jazz Band in the West Coast Lounge followed by a post-show film discussion.

title: Orpheum Tours
description: Vancouver Civic Theatres hosts 90-minute guided walking tours of the iconic Orpheum concert hall led by the BC Entertainment Hall of Fame. Guests explore the 1927 National Heritage Site and discover backstage secrets from its rich entertainment history.

title: VSO Masterworks: Prokofiev's Cinderella
description: The Vancouver Symphony Orchestra and conductor Antony Hermus perform a fairytale program featuring Scriabin's Rêverie, Shostakovich's First Violin Concerto with violinist Kevin Zhu, and Prokofiev's Cinderella Suite. Staged at the historic Orpheum Theatre in downtown Vancouver.

title: Stand Festival: Peru Vivo - Rhythm & Roots and Time in Two
description: The Stand Festival presents a dual dance showcase featuring ROOTS Peruvian Folk Dance exploring Peru's diverse cultural traditions alongside 'Time in Two' by Ukrainian street dance collaborators from Born II Boogie crew. The evening brings together dynamic folk choreography and contemporary street movement at the ANNEX.

title: Peru Vivo: Rhythm and Roots
description: ROOTS Peruvian Folk Dance presents a celebration of Peru’s cultural diversity, taking audiences on a journey through the Coast, Highlands, and Amazon regions. The dynamic performance features traditional costumes, storytelling, and energetic dances including Festejo, Polka, and Valicha.

title: Austentatious: An Improvised Jane Austen Novel
description: From London’s West End comes the smash-hit, long-form improv comedy where the all-star Austentatious cast improvises a new Jane Austen novel inspired by an audience title. Performed in period costume with live musical accompaniment, the acclaimed production features award-winning stars of the UK comedy scene.

title: VAM Symphony Orchestra: Legends of the Console
description: The VAM Symphony Orchestra celebrates iconic video game soundtracks from The Legend of Zelda, Skyrim, Super Mario, and more at the Orpheum. This concert takes audiences on a nostalgic journey celebrating beloved melodies from legendary gaming adventures.

title: Beck: Ride Lonesome Tour
description: Eight-time Grammy-winner Beck brings his Ride Lonesome Tour to the Queen Elizabeth Theatre with support from Ioanna Gika. The performance showcases his acclaimed catalog alongside original compositions.

title: Sunday Morning
description: An inclusive Sunday morning service welcoming people of all identities and spiritual backgrounds to explore progressive ideas and meaningful conversations. The gathering features diverse music spanning classical, contemporary, folk, gospel, jazz, and world styles.

title: Congregational Choir Rehearsal
description: Led by Choral Director Peggy Hua, this non-auditioned church choir rehearses a blend of classics and modern sacred music in the Sanctuary. Participation is open to the community with rehearsals supporting monthly Sunday morning performances.

title: Good News Cafe
description: A weekly community gathering for seniors exploring timely topics, sharing good news, and enjoying conversations over coffee. Held on Tuesday mornings in the Salons at St. Andrew's-Wesley United Church.

title: Parent & Tot
description: A weekly drop-in for newborns, toddlers, preschoolers, and their caregivers featuring free play, stories, parachute games, and singing in the Sanctuary. Special guests from the community also attend to share early childhood resources and healthcare information.

title: Ignite! Children’s Group
description: Ignite! is a welcoming, mid-week children’s and youth group offering a brave space for movement games, board games, creative art, music, and questions of faith. The session runs Tuesday evening in the Sanctuary and Salons at St. Andrew's-Wesley United Church.

title: West End Singers
description: West End Singers is a fun, free non-auditioned community choir at St. Andrew's-Wesley United Church led by Choral Director Peggy Hua. Open to all singing levels without music reading requirements, the group performs musical theatre, Broadway, pop, and film favourites every Wednesday.

title: Light and Shadow Bible Study
description: An Advent Bible study exploring the themes of light and shadow using a variety of scriptures. Participants reflect on where life is illuminated and draw nearer to the rebirth of Love.

title: West End Children’s Choir
description: A welcoming, secular community choir program for children ages 3 and up meeting weekly on Thursdays at St. Andrew's-Wesley United Church. Sessions are split into Musical Friends (ages 3 to Grade 1) and Singing Songbirds (Grades 2 and up) focusing on musical games, choral singing, and performance.

title: Remembrance Day Sunday
description: Join the Sunday morning Remembrance Day service honouring those who died in combat and war while praying for lasting peace. Featuring piper Cameron Bonar, trumpeter Brandon Walker, and music by the Sanctuary Singers.

title: Climate Talks: Hold Fast: How to Heal Personal and Climate Grief
description: Wendy Sarkissian launches three books in her Twilight River Trilogy, exploring personal and climate grief in a time of climate breakdown. The community event takes place in the Chapel at St. Andrew's-Wesley United Church.

title: Lights of Hope
description: Celebrate the Lights of Hope at St. Paul's with a warm community gathering featuring hot cocoa, cookies, and live music. Children are invited to participate in crafts while all guests share time in community at the St. Andrew's-Wesley Sanctuary.

title: Lifelines Poetry
description: Lifelines Poetry offers a safe, reflective space to read poetry and share thoughtful conversation. Open to all with no prior experience required, participants can register via email.

title: Spirit-given gifts workshop
description: Explore spiritual gifts and discover how to be a force for goodness and peace in the community through this intimate workshop. The program includes two Sunday sessions, lunch, and a one-on-one session with a minister.

title: Parent, Pie and Prayer
description: A night for parents to connect in conversation, listen to one another, and share in community with pie. Registration is free via email to St. Andrew's-Wesley United Church.

title: Poetry with Amy H.
description: A welcoming poetry workshop offering opportunities to explore poetry and exercise creativity in a supportive chapel setting. Hosted by Amy H. at St. Andrew's-Wesley United Church.

title: Invisible Rivers: Annie Bloch
description: Watch the pipe organ come to life under the control of organist and improviser Annie Bloch in partnership with Publik Secrets. Her composed improvisations explore states of change, drawing from experimental music as well as pop and ambient styles.

title: Break the Silence Series
description: Antiracism trainer Angela Ma Brown leads a combined worship and workshop session exploring how to build an inclusive and loving community. Attendees will develop new skills and engage in meaningful conversations to unpack racism.

title: Trans Day of Remembrance Vigil
description: A contemplative service for Trans Day of Remembrance commemorating transgender people lost to violence and honoring those working for trans rights. The vigil features music from Leo D.E Johnson and Matthew Presidente, alongside a reflection from Rev. Lauren Kirkey.

title: Word is OUT!
description: A safe and supportive community space exploring the intersections between faith and LGBT2Q+ identity. Features food, discussion, honesty, and spiritual fellowship held at St. Andrew's-Wesley United Church.

title: Stitching Circle
description: Join the Stitching Circle at St. Andrew's-Wesley United Church to knit, crochet, and build community together. The drop-in group meets twice a month in the Salons to create handcrafted items in a welcoming environment.

title: Eat Pray Love Christian New Year
description: A community gathering featuring music, prayer, storytelling, and creativity for all ages to celebrate the Christian New Year. The event includes a shared meal with registration requested via email.

title: Celebrating the start of the Advent Season
description: Celebrate the beginning of Advent with a simple lunch and craft activities at St. Andrew's-Wesley United Church. Attendees can create an Advent Wreath, decorate the church Christmas tree, and make ornaments.

title: Last Christian in Bethlehem Screening and Palestinian Art Market
description: Join St. Andrew's-Wesley United Church for a screening of the film Last Christian in Bethlehem followed by a talkback conversation. Attendees can also browse a Palestinian holiday market featuring works by Palestinian artists and makers before and after the screening.

title: I'm Going Through Some Things: A Solo Show by Ben Immanuel
description: Ben Immanuel brings the world premiere of his new one-man show, I'M GOING THROUGH SOME THINGS, to The Nest Theatre. The solo performance explores the challenges of facing life and mortality with wisdom, courage, and surrender.

title: 52 Stories
description: 52 Stories is a storytelling show taking place inside the memory palace of Pick-of-the-Fringe award-winning storyteller and improviser Dave Morris. Blending a memorization trick with heartfelt and heartbreaking personal stories, the performance explores themes of family, love, loss, and memory.

title: EQUUS by Peter Shaffer
description: After nearly 20 years, Peter Shaffer's Tony and Jessie Award-winning provocative psychological drama EQUUS returns to Vancouver for a one-week run. Staged at Granville Island's Performance Works, this bold revival features six limited performances.
restrictions: All Ages / Licensed events 19+ with 2 pieces of ID

title: Stuart Little
description: Carousel Theatre for Young People presents Joseph Robinette's stage adaptation of E.B. White's classic tale Stuart Little at the Waterfront Theatre. Stuart, an endearing mouse with a great big heart, navigates human adventures with courage, whimsy, and humor.

title: Pandemonium Pro and Dusk Pro presents- See You In Vancouver
description: Pandemonium Pro Wrestling makes its high-energy Canadian debut in Vancouver alongside Dusk Pro. Fans can expect three hours of hard-hitting indie wrestling action and memorable live entertainment.

title: Book Talk with Kevin Spenst – Stanley Park Manor: A Collective History
description: Celebrate local West End history with author Kevin Spenst as he shares stories and research from his new book recounting the hundred-year history of Stanley Park Manor. Accompanied by former building manager Lyn Guy sharing accounts of resident Enid Sheppard, the evening includes a short film, readings, Q&A, and complimentary tea and refreshments.

title: VICO Concert in the Parlour: Uzbek Musical Heritage
description: The Vancouver Inter-Cultural Orchestra presents an intimate concert of Uzbek musical heritage featuring chang master Ravshan Tukhtamishev in the Victorian parlour of Roedde House Museum. Complimentary tea and cookies are served following the performance.

title: Masterworks Diamond Series
description: The Vancouver Symphony Orchestra presents the Assante Vancouver Centre Masterworks Diamond Series at the Orpheum. This classical concert series features masterworks including Prokofiev's Cinderella, Grieg, Liszt, Mozart, Schumann, Wagner, and Mahler conducted by Otto Tausk and guest conductors.

title: Masterworks Gold | Liszt Piano Concerto No. 1
description: The Vancouver Symphony Orchestra performs Liszt's dramatic Piano Concerto No. 1 as part of the Masterworks Gold series at the historic Orpheum theatre. Featuring sweeping romantic orchestral compositions, this classical performance offers select orchestra seating starting at $50.00 CAD.

title: Masterworks Gold Series
description: The Vancouver Symphony Orchestra presents the Masterworks Gold Series at the Orpheum, featuring five major classical programs across Friday and Saturday evenings. Performances include works by Liszt, Brahms, Strauss, and Stravinsky alongside renowned international guest soloists and conductors.

title: November Chamber Players
description: The Vancouver Symphony Orchestra Chamber Players perform an intimate classical program at Pyatt Hall with general admission seating. Multiple concert dates and times are available across the November performance run.

title: Beethoven 1 & 3: Beginnings & Revolution
description: The Vancouver Symphony Orchestra performs Beethoven's Symphony No. 1 and Symphony No. 3 'Eroica' at the historic Orpheum Theatre. This performance traces Beethoven's path from classical beginnings to revolutionary symphonic masterworks.

title: Beethoven 2 & 7: Dance & Vitality
description: Experience Beethoven's uplifting Second and Seventh Symphonies performed live by the Vancouver Symphony Orchestra at the historic Orpheum. The performance celebrates rhythmic drive, dance, and symphonic vitality with seating options starting at $32.00.

title: Musically Speaking | Philip Glass & The Firebird
description: The Vancouver Symphony Orchestra presents Musically Speaking: Philip Glass & The Firebird at the Orpheum. A masterwork orchestral concert pairing contemporary minimalist brilliance with Stravinsky's dazzling classic.

title: VSO: Vivaldi’s The Four Seasons
venue: Chan Centre for the Performing Arts
description: The Vancouver Symphony Orchestra performs Vivaldi's masterwork, The Four Seasons, live at the Chan Centre for the Performing Arts. Experience this timeless classical journey across dynamic seasonal landscapes.

title: The Muppet Christmas Carol In Concert Live to Film
description: Experience The Muppet Christmas Carol projected on the big screen accompanied live by the Vancouver Symphony Orchestra at the Orpheum. A holiday cinematic concert featuring festive orchestral arrangements of classic songs.

title: Vienna After Beethoven
description: Part of the PARC Retirement Living Tea & Trumpets matinee series, the Vancouver Symphony Orchestra performs Vienna After Beethoven at the historic Orpheum Theatre. The program explores classical masterworks following the transformative era of Beethoven.

title: Tea & Trumpets
description: Enjoy an afternoon of classical music at the Orpheum mixed with entertaining stories and narration from host Christopher Gaze. Features performances by the Vancouver Symphony Orchestra with Resident Conductor Trevor Wilson.

title: Broadway Reimagined with Sarah Slean
description: Acclaimed vocalist and songwriter Sarah Slean joins the Vancouver Symphony Orchestra for an evening of reimagined Broadway classics at the historic Orpheum. The performance blends theatrical favorites with lush symphonic arrangements.

title: Kids Concerts: Peter and the Wolf
description: The Vancouver Symphony Orchestra presents Prokofiev's timeless orchestral fairy tale 'Peter and the Wolf' in this family-friendly Kids Concerts performance. Audiences of all ages can experience the magic of symphonic storytelling live at the Orpheum.

title: Kids Concerts Series
description: Concert experiences curated especially for young audience members featuring theatre, film, and dance with the Vancouver Symphony Orchestra. Performances take place on Sunday afternoons at the Orpheum with an interactive pre-concert playzone.

title: Masterworks Gold | Brahms, Sibelius & Debussy
description: The Vancouver Symphony Orchestra presents Masterworks Gold featuring classical masterworks by Brahms, Sibelius, and Debussy live at the Orpheum. Audiences can experience orchestral performances with accessible single-ticket pricing starting from $32.00.

title: Assante Masterworks Diamond | Grieg, Liszt, Fung & Strauss
description: The Vancouver Symphony Orchestra performs works by Grieg, Liszt, Fung, and Strauss as part of the Assante Masterworks Diamond series at the Orpheum. Multiple seating tiers starting at $32.00 offer an accessible gateway to an evening of world-class orchestral music.

title: Beethoven 4 & 5: Surprise & Destiny
description: The Vancouver Symphony Orchestra performs Beethoven's fourth and fifth symphonies at the historic Orpheum Theatre. An evening exploring surprise and destiny through two of the classical canon's most celebrated orchestral works.

title: Beethoven 6 & 8: Nature & Play
description: The Vancouver Symphony Orchestra performs Beethoven's Symphonies No. 6 and 8 in an afternoon concert exploring nature and musical play. Held at the historic Orpheum theatre in downtown Vancouver.

title: Musically Speaking | Rachmaninoff’s Third Piano Concerto
description: The Vancouver Symphony Orchestra presents Rachmaninoff's Third Piano Concerto as part of the Musically Speaking series at the historic Orpheum theatre. Featuring virtuoso orchestral performances with tickets starting at $32.00.

title: North Shore Classics Series
description: The PARC Retirement Living North Shore Classics series presents the Vancouver Symphony Orchestra performing classical masterworks at Centennial Theatre in North Vancouver. Featured concerts highlight Rachmaninoff's Third Piano Concerto and works by Mozart, Brahms, and Strauss.

title: PARC Retirement Living Tea & Trumpets | ¡Viva España!
description: The Vancouver Symphony Orchestra presents ¡Viva España! as part of the PARC Retirement Living Tea & Trumpets matinee series at the Orpheum. Audiences can enjoy vibrant Spanish-inspired orchestral classics in an afternoon concert setting.

title: Circus Incognitus
description: Part of the Vancouver Symphony Orchestra's Kids Concerts series, Circus Incognitus brings physical comedy and circus arts together with symphonic music at the historic Orpheum Theatre. A family-friendly Sunday afternoon performance with tiered seating available from $20.00 to $36.00.

title: Surrey Sundays Series
description: The Vancouver Symphony Orchestra presents the Surrey Sundays Series featuring classical masterworks performed live at the Bell Performing Arts Centre in Surrey. The season highlights renowned guest conductors and soloists alongside timeless works by Bach, Mozart, Rimsky-Korsakov, and Shostakovich.

title: Masterworks Gold | Strauss, Schumann & Respighi
description: The Vancouver Symphony Orchestra presents Masterworks Gold featuring works by Strauss, Schumann, and Respighi at the historic Orpheum Theatre. Audiences can experience a dynamic orchestral program with multiple seating tiers starting from $32.00.

title: Musically Speaking | Dvorák’s Cello Concerto
description: The Vancouver Symphony Orchestra performs Dvorák’s Cello Concerto as part of their Musically Speaking series at the historic Orpheum theatre. Audience members experience world-class orchestral performance with entry seating starting at $32.00 CAD.

title: Assante Masterworks Diamond | Mozart & Shostakovich 8
description: The Vancouver Symphony Orchestra performs Mozart & Shostakovich 8 as part of the Assante Masterworks Diamond series at the historic Orpheum. A masterwork orchestral showcase highlighting classical repertoire with accessible ticket options starting at $32.

title: PARC Retirement Living Tea & Trumpets | Gershwin’s Rhapsody in Blue
description: The Vancouver Symphony Orchestra performs Gershwin's iconic Rhapsody in Blue at the historic Orpheum as part of the Tea & Trumpets matinee series. Attendees can experience live symphonic jazz and classical mastery in an elegant afternoon concert setting.

title: London Drugs VSO Pops | The Music of Zimmer vs Williams
description: The Vancouver Symphony Orchestra performs iconic film scores celebrating cinematic titans Hans Zimmer and John Williams at the Orpheum. A symphonic pops concert spanning legendary movie themes with accessible seating options starting under $50 CAD.

title: Air China Classical Afterworks | Mozart, Brahms & Strauss
description: The Vancouver Symphony Orchestra presents an early evening Classical Afterworks concert featuring works by Mozart, Brahms, and Strauss at the historic Orpheum Theatre. Attendees can enjoy classical masterpieces starting at an accessible price point in the orchestra sections.

title: Kids Concerts | Beethoven Lives Upstairs!
description: The Vancouver Symphony Orchestra presents Beethoven Lives Upstairs as part of their Kids Concerts series at the Orpheum. A family-friendly symphonic performance exploring the life and music of Ludwig van Beethoven.

title: Assante Masterworks Diamond | Schumann & Wagner
description: The Vancouver Symphony Orchestra performs masterworks by Schumann and Wagner at the historic Orpheum Theatre as part of the Assante Masterworks Diamond series. Reserved seating tiers start at $32.00 CAD, providing an accessible classical concert experience in downtown Vancouver.

title: April Chamber Players
description: The Vancouver Symphony Orchestra Chamber Players perform an intimate classical repertoire at Pyatt Hall. Seating for this performance is general admission.

title: Masterworks Gold | Brahms & Dvořák 8
description: The Vancouver Symphony Orchestra performs Masterworks Gold featuring the symphonic masterpieces of Brahms and Dvořák's Symphony No. 8 at the historic Orpheum Theatre. Ticket prices begin at $32.00 for balcony and orchestra seating tiers.

title: Disney and Pixar’s Up In Concert Live to Film
description: Experience Disney and Pixar’s beloved animated classic Up accompanied by the Vancouver Symphony Orchestra performing the score live to film. The performance takes place at the historic Orpheum theatre in downtown Vancouver.

title: Jan Lisiecki Plays Beethoven’s Emperor
description: Acclaimed pianist Jan Lisiecki joins the Vancouver Symphony Orchestra at the historic Orpheum to perform Beethoven’s triumphant Piano Concerto No. 5 'Emperor'. A masterwork of classical repertoire presented as part of the VSO concert season.

title: Musically Speaking | Mozart, Bartók & Ligeti
description: The Vancouver Symphony Orchestra performs works by Mozart, Bartók, and Ligeti at the historic Orpheum Theatre as part of the Musically Speaking series. Seats start from $32.00 across orchestra and balcony sections.

title: Natural Woman: Sheléa Sings Aretha Franklin
description: Vocal powerhouse Sheléa joins the Vancouver Symphony Orchestra for London Drugs VSO Pops, celebrating the music and legacy of Aretha Franklin. The performance brings iconic hits and soulful arrangements to the historic Orpheum stage.

title: Kids Concerts | M is for Mystery
description: Part of the Vancouver Symphony Orchestra's Kids Concerts series, 'M is for Mystery' invites young audiences and families to an engaging symphonic performance at the historic Orpheum Theatre. Attendees can experience live orchestral storytelling with accessible seat selections starting at $20.

title: Masterworks Gold | Stravinsky’s Petrushka
description: The Vancouver Symphony Orchestra performs Stravinsky's vivid masterpiece Petrushka as part of the Masterworks Gold series at the Orpheum. This concert highlights dynamic orchestral storytelling with affordable entry-level seating options starting under fifty dollars.

title: Elgar’s Violin & Mahler 10
description: The Vancouver Symphony Orchestra performs Elgar’s Violin Concerto alongside Mahler’s Symphony No. 10 at the historic Orpheum theatre as part of the Assante Masterworks Diamond series. Ticket options start from $32.00 for reserved seating.

title: Beethoven 9: Ode to Joy
description: Experience Beethoven's monumental Symphony No. 9 'Ode to Joy' presented by the Vancouver Symphony Orchestra live at the historic Orpheum. Featuring soaring choral movements and world-class orchestral performance, this concert offers accessible entry pricing starting at $32.00 CAD.

title: June Chamber Players
description: June Chamber Players perform live in concert at Pyatt Hall with general admission seating. Presented as part of the Vancouver Symphony Orchestra's chamber series.

title: M is for Mystery - Elementary School Concerts
description: VSO Elementary school concerts introduce K-7 students to orchestral music through an interactive 45-minute musical mystery quest. Whimsical and surprising, M is for Mystery explores the joy of discovery and the magic of symphonic music at The Orpheum.

title: Symphonic Encounters: Beethoven 1 & 3: Beginnings & Revolution
description: The VSO's open rehearsal program, Symphonic Encounters, invites students, teachers, and community groups behind the scenes at the Orpheum Theatre to experience regular professional rehearsals. Attendees can also participate in musician Q&As and guided venue tours.

title: Jean Coulthard Readings and Mentorship Program
description: The Jean Coulthard Readings and Mentorship Program offers emerging Canadian composers guidance and mentorship from the Vancouver Symphony Orchestra. The program culminates in a final reading session and recording of participating composers' works at the Annex Theatre.

title: Bonnes Bonnes
description: Touchstone Theatre and Théâtre la Seizième present Bonnes Bonnes with performances offered in both English and French. The production is featured as part of the 2026-2027 mainstage theatre season in Vancouver.

title: Behind the Moon
description: In a Mughlai restaurant in Toronto, Ayub is forced to confront reality and abandoned dreams when a mysterious cab driver walks in one night. Written by Anosh Irani, this drama explores love, loss, and beginning again.

title: Jonathan Van Ness
venue: Chan Shun Concert Hall at Chan Performing Arts Centre
description: Jonathan Van Ness delivers a high-energy live stage performance combining visual storytelling, music, and distinctive theatrical presentation. The touring production adapts to the Chan Shun Concert Hall for an audience-focused experience suitable for all ages.

title: Disney On Ice: Jump In!
description: Disney On Ice: Jump In! brings beloved Disney stories to life on ice with world-class figure skating, music, and immersive production design. The North American tour visits Vancouver's Pacific Coliseum with multiple performance dates and affordable admission options.

title: Parallelogram Volume 2: Presence
description: Volume 2 of The Polygon Gallery's digital exhibition Parallelogram addresses the theme of 'presence' and how we situate ourselves online and offline. The online presentation brings together works by Indigenous artists linking land, place, memory, and futurity through visual media, video, and poetry.

title: Kids First
description: Kids First invites children and families to get creative on the first weekend of the month with hands-on art-making and fun activities at The Polygon Gallery. Admission is by donation courtesy of BMO, with advance registration welcomed and walk-ins invited all day.

title: House of R3nc0ng: Queer Worldbuilding Amidst the Fire
description: Indonesian filmmaker and researcher Rizky Rahad joins The Polygon Gallery for an artist talk and special screening of his film House of R3nc0ng, exploring queer cinema as rebellious worldmaking. Followed by a talkback moderated by Love Intersections, admission is free by donation with RSVPs requested.

title: when the one to author the cut is gone a hole in the shape of a portal forms
description: Vuntut Gwitchin interdisciplinary artist Jeneen Frei Njootli and their father Stanley Njootli Sr. present a transformative performance relating to the Knowledge Transference IV work. Admission to The Polygon Gallery is always by donation, with RSVPs encouraged for this evening event.

title: Exhibitions at The Polygon Gallery
description: The Polygon Gallery presents contemporary visual arts and photography exhibitions alongside public engagement programs on the North Vancouver waterfront. General gallery admission is open to the public and provided by donation.

title: The Lind Biennial Opening Celebration
description: Join The Polygon Gallery for the opening celebration of The Lind Biennial, honouring emerging BC-based artists working in photography, film, and video. The evening features a public reception at 7:00 PM followed by opening remarks at 7:30 PM.

title: Son of a Preacherman
description: Written and performed by Ins Choi (creator of Kim's Convenience), this heartfelt and funny solo performance blends storytelling, spoken word, and live music from a three-piece band exploring faith and creativity. All listed tour showings are currently sold out.

title: Christmas Presence
description: PT’s beloved holiday variety program debuts at the Revue Stage on Granville Island, featuring a thoughtful mix of stories, poetry, and music. Each performance is unique, with nightly line-up changes of actors, writers, and musicians.

title: Mental
description: Mental is a raw and deeply personal new work by Vancouver playwright Jill Daum depicting a mother's fierce fight to protect her child. Directed by Kaitlin Williams and starring Anita Wittenberg, this world premiere drama runs 80 minutes without intermission.

title: That Green Ideal: Emily Carr and the Idea of Nature
description: The largest solo exhibition of iconic British Columbia artist Emily Carr at the Vancouver Art Gallery in over twenty years, featuring more than 100 works exploring her obsession with the Pacific Northwest landscape. Curated by Richard Hill and Andrea Valentine-Lewis, the showcase investigates how Carr understood nature, romantic transcendence, and her relation to Indigenous cultures.

title: Modern Iran and the Avant-Gardes, 1948–78
description: Modern Iran and the Avant-Gardes, 1948–78 explores how complex cultural tensions in post-war Iran led to groundbreaking artistic innovation. The exhibition presents approximately 100 works across painting, sculpture, photography, and mixed media by influential modernist Iranian artists.

title: Vancouver Now! Annie Briard
description: As part of the Vancouver Now! exhibition series, Annie Briard presents an immersive sensory installation challenging traditional frameworks of perception through light, space, and lens-based media. The site-responsive environment invites visitors into a slower, heightened awareness of how we see, interpret, and experience the world.

title: Made in Hong Kong: From the Collection
description: Featuring works from approximately 35 artists drawn from the permanent collection, this exhibition maps Hong Kong's creative evolution across six decades of modern and contemporary art. It explores the city's dynamic visual culture through painting, ink art, photography, video, and installation.

title: Vancouver Now! Manjot Kaur
description: Spotlighting third featured artist Manjot Kaur in the Gallery's ongoing Vancouver Now! series, combining Indian miniature painting traditions with sound installations of endangered birds. Her speculative hybrid beings explore Hindu female deities, feminist ecologies, and planetary coexistence.

title: True Story!
description: Audience members share real-life stories that the cast transforms into fast, hilarious improvised scenes. In the second half, performers tell their own stories in a classic Armando-style format for an evening of heartfelt and comedic storytelling.

title: The Ornament Collection
venue: Craft Council of BC Shop & Gallery
description: The Craft Council of BC presents The Ornament Collection, an annual festive fundraiser and curated exhibition showcasing handcrafted ornaments by artists across British Columbia. Hosted at the Craft Council of BC Shop & Gallery on Granville Island, the exhibition runs throughout the holiday season with free public access.

title: Granville Island Remembers
description: A Remembrance Day ceremony on Granville Island featuring the Last Post played by Anita Eccleston followed by a moment of silence and reflection. Lone bagpiper Anthony Warburton signals the conclusion with Flowers of the Forest.

title: Infidels Jazz Presents: Casey Thomas-Burns Sings Ella X-Mas
description: Vocalist and trombonist Casey Thomas-Burns and her band bring the classic holiday album 'Ella Wishes You a Swinging Christmas' to live audiences at The Revue Stage. Join Infidels Jazz to celebrate Ella Fitzgerald's iconic festive music and ring in the season with joy.

title: Ambient States
description: An intimate evening of deep listening and meditation featuring original ambient music and field recordings by Kasia. The performance is accompanied by real-time audio-reactive visual projections by Laser Tech.

title: Melt II: Membrane
description: Melt II: Membrane is the second chapter of the immersive electronic club series exploring atmospheric soundscapes and heavy bass. Headlined by Maude Vôs alongside Xiumei, IHA, ephemeral objects, Gwaimui, and Tucy at a secret Vancouver location.

title: Echo Locations presents: Reflexions
description: Echo Locations relaunches its intimate Reflexions underground series in Vancouver featuring uptempo dub techno and hypnotic electronic selections. The night showcases live and DJ sets from Antonio Elgeta, AWood, and niki disc.

title: VANTEK: DJ SWISHA
description: VANTEK and RUFFNECK SOUND present DJ SWISHA in Vancouver, blending club music, Jersey club, house, and bass-heavy sounds with rhythm at the center. Supported by Deluge, Kraang, Mozya, and Star Girl for an all-night underground event.

title: Devours (Live) with shyperv
description: Devours performs live with support from shyperv at the Biltmore Cabaret in East Vancouver's Mount Pleasant neighbourhood. The 19+ Sunday evening show runs from 7:00 PM to 11:00 PM with tickets starting at $10.

title: An Evening of Live Electronic Music with Jay Hosking, Dasine, SEQNK, tafony
description: Conduit Gallery presents four live electronic sets spanning techno, drum & bass, and hardstyle. The lineup features Jay Hosking, Dasine, SEQNK, and tafony for a 19+ night in Vancouver.

Textures presents 001 featuring sets by Pink-E & Brane, Oscar, and Deckard at Platform9 in Vancouver. The underground club night showcases drum & bass, jungle, and dubplate pressure from 10:00 PM to 4:00 AM.

title: Innellea (Vancouver)
description: Innellea returns to Vancouver for a Playhouse Saturday takeover at Celebrities Night Club. The night features melodic house and tech house selections running from 10:00 PM to 4:00 AM.

title: Propagate Pres. Doss & CFCF
description: Shapeshifters CFCF and Doss take over Fortune Sound Club for an electric, high-energy double headliner spanning house, electroclash, and maximalist dance. Expect heady DJ sets in Chinatown powered by Fortune's signature Funktion-One sound system.

title: SUBculture Saturdays: Alix Perez
description: Producer, DJ, and 1985 Music founder Alix Perez brings his signature spectrum of drum & bass, halftime, and deep bass music to SUBculture Saturdays. Held at The Red Room in Vancouver with local support to be announced.

title: VANTEK: Chris Liebing
description: Techno pioneer Chris Liebing returns to Vancouver for an extended three-hour set exploring driving, stripped-back soundscapes. He is joined for the all-night underground event by local support from Son Of Magnus and Night Format.

title: Disco Affair
description: An intimate evening of 70s disco, funk, and boogie in a private hidden room at Chinatown cocktail bar Meo. Features music curated by DJAJ and includes a welcome drink with admission.

title: Club Fiction: The Afterparty
description: Club Fiction keeps the energy going after Sammy Virji's PNE Forum show with an unofficial afterparty celebrating the UKG revival wave. Featuring a lineup of local talent including Mole, Labwrks, and Geerlinks at 520 Alexander Street in Railtown.

title: Little Ravers: (Vancouver)
description: Little Ravers brings an all-ages family dance party featuring local DJs spinning house, garage, and kid-friendly remixes. The high-energy gathering combines face painting, inflatables, and live entertainers with full bar amenities for parents.

title: Surrey Sundays | Mozart, Bartók & Ligeti
description: The Vancouver Symphony Orchestra performs a Sunday matinee of classical and twentieth-century masterworks by Mozart, Bartók, and Ligeti at the Bell Performing Arts Centre in Surrey.

title: Dracula: A Comedy of Terrors
venue: Lindsay Family Stage at Granville Island
description: Everyone knows the story: a vampiric count, a kidnapped young lady, and a brave hero to save the day. But this time around, the hero’s a coward, the lady yearns for adventure, and the count is…a cake-baking dreamboat? This Dracu-larious adaptation of the gothic classic gleefully turns the tale on its head but never loses track of its heart—that’s where the stake goes, after all. Whether you’re an eternal vampire-lover or a fresh fan of fangs, you can definitely count on a scarily fun time.

title: FROM THE DEEP: In the Wake of Drexciya with Ayana V. Jackson
description: In her first major institutional exhibition, American artist Ayana V. Jackson draws inspiration from the mythic underwater world imagined by Detroit techno duo Drexciya to create a feminist, Pan-African aquatopia inhabited by water spirits from African and Afro-Atlantic traditions. Through photography, immersive video, animation, and installation, From the Deep unfolds as an enchanting, contemplative environment that transforms the Atlantic Ocean from a site of trauma brought by the slave trade to a realm of speculative fiction.

title: Opening Celebrations of From the Deep: In the Wake of Drexciya
description: Celebrate the opening of MOA's new feature exhibition, From the Deep: In the Wake of Drexciya with Ayana V. Jackson. Enjoy free museum admission, opening remarks from the artist, and music by DJ Nea. Light refreshments served.

title: Visual + Material Culture Research Seminar Series – Fall 2026
description: This interdisciplinary seminar series is for anyone with interests in visual and material culture across different departments at UBC and beyond. The seminar provides an opportunity to share research and exchange ideas, usually followed by conversations over a drink at Koerner’s Pub. Open to students, staff, faculty and community members in and around UBC.

description: It is a rock outcropping in Stanley Park. A legend among the Indigenous Squamish people surrounds the rock. It is between 15 and 18 metres (49 and 59 ft) tall. It became known to mariners as Nine Pin Rock for its resemblance to a bowling pin.

title: Cirque du Soleil: Luzia
description: Join us as we take you on a journey into the colorful and fantastical world of LUZIA, set in a make-believe Mexico, where you will be treated to stunning visual surprises and breathtaking acrobatic performances. LUZIA deftly guides you through the locations, people, and sounds of both classical and contemporary Mexico, taking you from urban locations like an old movie set and a smoke-filled dance hall to the beach and barren desert.

title: FAN EXPO Vancouver
description: Three days of fun-filled, fan culture! If you're into comics, sci-fi, horror, anime, gaming, or cosplay, come share our playground. You'll feel out of this world – and right at home. Find your fandom family at FAN EXPO Vancouver. All 35,000 of them.

title: The Basement Yard Live
description: The Basement Yard is back with a brand new live show that’s bigger, bolder, and more interactive than ever. Joe Santagato and Frank Alvarez bring their unfiltered hot takes, heated debates, and hilarious crowd participation to the stage, turning each night into an unforgettable experience. Joe Santagato has partnered with PLUS1 so that $1 from every ticket sold goes to The Happy Cry Fund.
